messages.subject: Call for testing
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

It's about time to release a new version of RKWard, and we need your
help for testing. For those, who have not been following the
development, the key feature to look out for is that RKWard can now use
kate plugins. Importantly, this brings a much awaited "Search in
Files"-feature, but also many other goodies such as "Project"
management for source repositories, and Previews for bibtex referennces.

Beyond this, code completion features have been improved in the R
Console window, and a first run wizard now checks for common setup
issues.

A tentative release timeline with further links can be found at
https://rkward.kde.org/Release_Schedule.html . The most important
download links are also given, below.

Thanks!
Thomas

-- Mac users (and anybody with access to a Mac) --
- Get the latest DMG from
  https://binary-factory.kde.org/view/MacOS/job/RKWard_Nightly_macos/

- You will have to install R, separately (if you don't already have it).
  Currently any version between 3.4 and 3.6 should work. I'm planning
  to update the requirement to 4.0.0 and higher before the release,
  though.

- No further configuration should be needed. RKWard should detect the
  newest version of R installed.

-- Windows users --
- Get the latest installer from
  https://binary-factory.kde.org/view/Windows%20MingW/job/RKWard_Nightly_mingw64/

- R 4.0.2 is included in the bundle. You should be able to start RKWard
  right away. (Actually, it's R 3.6.2 right now, but will be R 4.0.2 on
  tomorrow's build).

- If you have a separate version of R installed on this machine, please
  also try the following: Edit the rkward.ini file (inside the
  "bin" folder of your RKWard installation), changing the content to "R
  executable=auto". In theory this should detect your external R
  installation and use that.

-- Linux / BSD users --
- Compile the lastest git master version from source, or install one of
  the nightly builds, if we provide one for your distribution
  (https://rkward.kde.org/RKWard_Source_Repository.html).

- Should you have several versions of R installed, try
  switching between versions using the --r-executable commandline
  parameter.

messages.subject: Using Ctags in rkward
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I was wondering if it is possible to use Ctags in rkward or if anyone 
has already been able to make it work.

Some context: CTags is a tool that can make your text editor 
"understand" code. In particular, it can be used to jump from a function 
call to the function definition. I was trying to enable Ctags support in 
rkward using the Ctags plugin for Kate; in vanilla Kate, this worked for 
me. That is, when I open an R project in Kate, I can jump from a line 
where a function is called to the function definition, even across 
files. (It was necessary to first add R language support, which is 
however easily done, for example as described here: 
https://tinyheero.github.io/2017/05/13/r-vim-ctags.html.) To me, this 
functionality is really useful, especially when developing an R package 
where I use many files to hold my R code.

In rkward, I can in principle activate the Ctags plugin, via *configure 
rkward -> Kate plugins*, but I did not find out how to actually use 
Ctags afterwards. In Kate, I could define key bindings for the Ctags 
plugin, but in rkward the "katectags" option is missing under the 
keybinding customization menu. So, to make Ctags work under rkward, I 
guess it would be necessary to include the "katectags" plugin options 
under the keybindings menu, if that is possible. In kate, the Ctags 
plugin can also be used when using the right mouse in the text editor, 
but this also seems not to be enabled in rkward.

I think that being able to use Ctags in rkward would be really great for 
R package development, and given that it is possible in Kate, it might 
also be possible to port this functionality to rkward? What do you guys 
think?

Cheers,

Martin

messages.subject: Using Ctags in rkward
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Am Wed, 28 Oct 2020 15:01:38 +0100
schrieb Martin Papenberg <martin.papenberg at uni-duesseldorf.de>:
> I was wondering if it is possible to use Ctags in rkward or if anyone 
> has already been able to make it work.

as a quick feedback, I can see the problem. Not sure on the best
solution, yet.

If you feel like some experimenting, try commenting out this line in
the sources:

https://invent.kde.org/education/rkward/-/blob/releases/0.7.2/rkward/windows/katepluginintegration.cpp#L517

This will make kate plugin actions appear regardless of the context
(importantly, also while the corresponding tool window is inactive).

I don't think that is a good solution, but maybe, instead, I can make it
so that kate plugin actions will be active whenever a script window is
active.

Regards
Thomas
